title: Nebula Systems - Private VPC discovery
summary: Initial discovery focused on Private VPC deployment, networking (VPC peering, PrivateLink, TGW), region constraints (us-east-1), KMS/HSM requirements, audit/log forwarding, and pilot timeline. Agreed next steps for security docs, Terraform module, and perf testing.
next_steps: Jordan to send SOC 2 + security pack and network onboarding doc by 2027-07-14
Priya to schedule technical deep dive + perf test with Maya for week of 2027-07-19
Customer to share VPC CIDR ranges and AWS account IDs for whitelisting by 2027-07-16
Jordan to provide pricing options for Private vs Dedicated by 2027-07-14
action_items: Jordan Meyers: Send SOC2, network onboarding guide, and draft pricing - due 2027-07-14
Priya Shah: Set up technical deep-dive and perf test plan; collect sample workload - due 2027-07-19
Maya Patel: Share VPC CIDR, account IDs, and proposed peering route table - due 2027-07-16
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-07-12 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (CTO), Maya Patel (Head of DevOps), Daniel Wu (Security), Sophie Lee (Procurement)

00:00 Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check, is this still a good time?
00:06 Alex Romero: Yeah all good, thanks Jordan.
00:10 Jordan Meyers: Awesome. Quick agenda, we wanted to understand your infra constraints for Private deployment — VPC peering, private endpoints, regions, and security controls. Priya will jump into technical questions.
00:20 Priya Shah: Hi team, thanks. Maya can you give us a brief on your current cloud footprint and networking?
00:28 Maya Patel: Sure. We're primarily on AWS in us-east-1 and us-west-2. Planning to keep most workloads in us-east-1. We run in a shared VPC, but for this project we want isolated VPCs per environment, production in a separate account.
00:42 Priya Shah: Got it. Do you have a transit gateway or are you using VPC peering?
00:46 Maya Patel: We use a TGW for most inter-VPC traffic. For third-party integrations we prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on the vendor.
00:55 Daniel Wu: From security, we need all data egress to be controlled; any private endpoints should terminate inside our VPC. We also require KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
01:08 Jordan Meyers: That makes sense. On Redwood Private we support a VPC deployment model where our inference nodes sit inside your VPC (customer-managed subnets) and we can talk via interface endpoints / PrivateLink or through an IPsec VPN if needed.
01:22 Alex Romero: Clarify terms — when you say "inside our VPC" do you mean we host the instances or you deploy within our account?
01:28 Priya Shah: Two patterns: 1) We deploy in your account as a private deployment (we ship a control plane that can be customer managed or a lightweight control plane with private control plane options), or 2) Dedicated but in our managed account with VPC peering to your environment. For strict data residency you usually want the deployment in your account.
01:46 Maya Patel: We prefer deployment inside our account. So we'd want clarity on required IAM roles, images, and whether we need a bastion.
01:55 Priya Shah: For deployment in your account, we provide an IaC template (CloudFormation/Terraform) to create the necessary resources: subnets (private), security groups, IAM roles, and optionally an S3 VPC endpoint for model artifacts. The nodes will live in private subnets with NAT for egress unless you want VPC endpoints for S3.
02:12 Maya Patel: Ok, S3 access needs to be via VPC endpoint. No public internet egress for model artifacts.
02:18 Daniel Wu: And KMS — we need CMKs in our account. Can the service use our KMS keys for data at rest?
02:24 Priya Shah: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest. We can integrate using cross-account access or deploy within your account so keys are local.
02:33 Alex Romero: What about private endpoints — do you use AWS PrivateLink or do you require routing changes?
02:38 Priya Shah: We support AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for control plane API endpoints. For data plane traffic between your services and the inference nodes, if deployed in your account, it's regular VPC internal routing. If we deploy outside your account, we can use VPC peering or TGW attachment depending on scale.
02:58 Maya Patel: For peering, we have strict CIDR allocation, our prod VPC is 10.10.0.0/16. Any requirements?
03:05 Priya Shah: No specific CIDR required but we recommend non-overlapping ranges. For peering with Redwood-managed account we will propose a peering CIDR.
03:12 Jordan Meyers: Also, for high throughput inference we recommend dedicated ENIs and enhanced networking; Priya will go into perf implications.
03:20 Priya Shah: Right. For latency-sensitive workloads we typically colocate in the same AZ if possible. If you need multi-AZ high availability, we distribute workers across AZs — but that adds cross-AZ traffic and minor latency.
03:35 Alex Romero: Are there region constraints? We need all processing in us-east-1 only.
03:40 Priya Shah: We can pin deployments to a single region per private deployment. If you want multiple regions we can replicate.
03:47 Daniel Wu: Compliance side — do you have SOC 2, and do you provide audit logs of model access and admin actions?
03:55 Jordan Meyers: Yes, we are SOC 2 compliant; I'll send the SOC 2 report. We also provide audit logs for admin operations and option to forward logs to your CloudWatch/CloudTrail or external SIEM via Kinesis/Logstash.
04:11 Maya Patel: How does networking for updates/patches work? Patching the nodes may require connections out to package repos.
04:18 Priya Shah: Agents use SSM or a pre-approved patching flow; we can restrict egress to specific endpoints or allow a bastion host to mediate. We can also ship patched AMIs to your account to avoid outbound access.
04:31 Sophie Lee: From procurement, price is a big factor — is Private much more than Dedicated?
04:36 Jordan Meyers: Private includes an onboarding and support fee plus infra usage. Dedicated is managed by Redwood in our accounts — cost depends on committed capacity. We'll provide a pricing comparison doc.
04:48 Alex Romero: Performance testing — can we run a perf benchmark with our prompts and models?
04:53 Priya Shah: Absolutely. We can run a perf test in a sandbox VPC or run the same workload on a small pilot deployment in your account. We'll collect latency, throughput, token pricing.
05:06 Maya Patel: For egress to S3 for embeddings and artifacts, we need interface endpoints and VPC endpoint policies. Can you include policies in the IaC?
05:15 Priya Shah: Yes, the Terraform module includes endpoint creation and sample endpoint policies. We can customize to your policy.
05:22 Daniel Wu: We also need RBAC and SSO — SAML integration required. Does your control plane support SAML with SCIM provisioning?
05:30 Jordan Meyers: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the console. We'll include docs.
05:37 Alex Romero: Any data residency concerns if you pin to us-east-1?
05:41 Priya Shah: If you pin everything to us-east-1 and deploy in your account, all data and logs remain in your region and account. Our control plane options allow private control plane too.
05:50 Maya Patel: Network ops question: route propagation for TGW — will Redwood request route table changes?
05:55 Priya Shah: If using TGW, we'll ask for specific route propagation to reach the subnets. We provide the exact CIDR ranges and ENI IPs ahead of time so you can add routes.
06:07 Sophie Lee: Timeline — we're looking to start a pilot in August. Is that feasible?
06:12 Jordan Meyers: Yes, pilot in August is feasible. We'll aim for network onboarding and security approvals mid-July so devs can start in August.
06:20 Alex Romero: Any limitations on NAT vs no-NAT deployments?
06:24 Priya Shah: We support both; if you go NAT-less, you'll need endpoints for all required services. The IaC can set that up.
06:31 Daniel Wu: We also need mention of HSM for key storage — do you support customer HSM integration?
06:36 Priya Shah: We integrate with customer KMS; for HSM-level keys we can discuss a proxy approach — it's a bit more custom but possible. We'll escalate if needed.
06:48 Maya Patel: Ok, can you also share the Terraform module and the list of required IAM permissions?
06:53 Jordan Meyers: Yes, I'll share the module link and a least-privilege permission set.
06:58 Priya Shah: For perf numbers, what latency SLO are you targeting?
07:02 Alex Romero: Sub-200ms for small completions (short prompts) and under 1s for larger prompt/response pairs would be ideal.
07:11 Priya Shah: We'll capture that in the perf test. For sub-200ms we may need model selection and quantized weights; we'll recommend appropriate instance types.
07:21 Maya Patel: Any multitenancy concerns in your managed account model?
07:25 Jordan Meyers: In managed account model, we isolate workloads via VPCs and IAM but some customers prefer full account deployment for strict separation.
07:34 Daniel Wu: On logging retention, we need 7 years for audit logs — can Redwood forward logs to our S3 with lifecycle policies?
07:41 Priya Shah: Yes, we can forward and configure retention in your account.
07:45 Alex Romero: Great. Let's recap next steps.
07:49 Jordan Meyers: Recap: I'll send SOC 2, security pack, Terraform module, and pricing by 2027-07-14. Priya will schedule a deep technical session and perf plan for week of 7/19. Maya will share VPC CIDR and AWS account IDs by 7/16. Does that look right?
08:06 Maya Patel: Yes that's correct.
08:09 Sophie Lee: From procurement we'll review the pricing doc and come back with questions.
08:13 Jordan Meyers: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the tech deep-dive.
08:18 Alex Romero: Thanks, bye.
08:20 End of transcript.
